Simulate buying and selling Gold (XAU) with $100,000 in virtual cash. Charts and prices are for education only — no real money, no brokerage relationship.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

What Gold is

Gold is a precious metal used in jewellery, industry and official reserves. TradeHQ's gold-labelled practice instrument can use CoinGecko PAX Gold (PAXG) token quotes as a price proxy, rather than a dedicated XAU/USD spot feed. PAXG volume and market cap refer to the token, not the global physical-gold market. Fixed fallback prices and separately labelled generated charts may also appear. A virtual holding acquires no physical gold, fund units or tokens.

Reference facts
Asset Class: Commodity
Correlation: Relationship varies by period
How to practise it here

Educational example: Analyze gold price action during periods of high CPI data, Fed policy shifts, or stock market volatility. Focus on real yields as a key driver. (Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

Asset-specific worksheet (hypothetical)

Compare a gram of physical gold, a fund share and a gold futures contract. List custody, expenses and settlement obligations separately. Mark these as distinct exposures: buying the simplified practice symbol does not acquire any of them.

Why learners study Gold

Gold has been used as a store of value for thousands of years and is often discussed as a hedge during uncertainty. Practising here shows how an asset can respond to fear and interest rates rather than earnings.

What tends to move Gold

Real interest rates, the US dollar, central-bank purchases and geopolitical tension are the drivers most commonly cited. Gold produces no income, so higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding it.

Gold: practice versus a real account

Owning physical gold involves storage, insurance and dealer spreads; gold funds and futures carry their own costs. A simulator shows only the price.

Common questions about trading Gold
How does Gold react during market crashes? — Gold and stock prices can respond differently across periods. A practice chart is simulated and does not establish an inverse relationship or reproduce a market crash.
How to practice gold trading for free as a student? — TradeHQ provides $100K virtual cash for gold (XAU) practice. Compare gains and losses under different price assumptions; gold is not a guaranteed hedge against inflation or market stress.
What factors can affect gold prices? — Real interest rates, the US dollar, central-bank demand, inflation expectations and geopolitical events are commonly discussed factors. Their effects are not fixed, so compare them over clearly stated periods.
Is gold trading good for learning macro analysis? — Gold can be used to study supply, demand, interest-rate and currency hypotheses. Its reaction to inflation or geopolitical news is uncertain rather than reliably directional.
A practice checklist for Gold
Check the direction of the US dollar before entering.
Note any upcoming interest-rate decision.
Write down whether you are hedging another practice position or speculating.

Asset-specific worksheet (hypothetical)

Compare a gram of physical gold, a fund share and a gold futures contract. List custody, expenses and settlement obligations separately. Mark these as distinct exposures: buying the simplified practice symbol does not acquire any of them.

Why learners study Gold

Gold has been used as a store of value for thousands of years and is often discussed as a hedge during uncertainty. Practising here shows how an asset can respond to fear and interest rates rather than earnings.

What tends to move Gold

Real interest rates, the US dollar, central-bank purchases and geopolitical tension are the drivers most commonly cited. Gold produces no income, so higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding it.

Gold: practice versus a real account

Owning physical gold involves storage, insurance and dealer spreads; gold funds and futures carry their own costs. A simulator shows only the price.

Common questions about trading Gold
How does Gold react during market crashes? — Gold and stock prices can respond differently across periods. A practice chart is simulated and does not establish an inverse relationship or reproduce a market crash.
How to practice gold trading for free as a student? — TradeHQ provides $100K virtual cash for gold (XAU) practice. Compare gains and losses under different price assumptions; gold is not a guaranteed hedge against inflation or market stress.
What factors can affect gold prices? — Real interest rates, the US dollar, central-bank demand, inflation expectations and geopolitical events are commonly discussed factors. Their effects are not fixed, so compare them over clearly stated periods.
Is gold trading good for learning macro analysis? — Gold can be used to study supply, demand, interest-rate and currency hypotheses. Its reaction to inflation or geopolitical news is uncertain rather than reliably directional.

Check the direction of the US dollar before entering.
Note any upcoming interest-rate decision.
Write down whether you are hedging another practice position or speculating.
